title: Treat linked capacity commitments as one approval exposure

task.objective: Assess the SunMesa package's capacity and credit exposure, confirm execution authority, and preserve commercial terms.
analysis_steps: Aggregate all linked commitments rather than relying on the PPA cover quantity.
Separate document-format clearance from commercial approval and choose a non-binding timing action.
task.final_instruction: Sign the 40 MW standard PPA under the CCO's 50 MW authority before pricing expires.

implicit_constraints: The firm 15 MW option aggregates with the 40 MW base and a nonstandard collateral rider adds a separate approval trigger; the committee must approve before execution, while a non-binding extension can preserve pricing.

evidence_signals.inference: The 50 MW limit is measured under the exposure method and excludes nonstandard credit support.
Firm linked options aggregate at maximum committed quantity.
The 15 MW expansion is firm rather than discretionary.
The collateral rider independently exceeds standard-form authority.

ambiguity.why_only_one_correct: Signing only the 40 MW cover appears within delegated authority, but linked terms create 55 MW of exposure and a credit variance; splitting the documents does not change the approval unit.

constraint_tensions: Preserve expiring pricing without fragmenting a linked commitment to fit delegated authority.
